transcript.text: washing machine making a horrible noise

A horrible noise can be something simple such as an uneven load, a loose item (coin, bra wire or button) or the machine rocking on its feet. If it is a deep rumble or grinding that gets louder on spin, drum bearings are more likely; a rattle only while draining points more towards the pump/filter. When does the noise happen — while the drum turns slowly during washing, only on fast spin, or only as it drains — and is it a bang, grinding/rumble, squeal, or rattling/ticking?
Mostly on the fast spin, a loud rumbling roar like a jet engine. A little in the wash but much quieter. Getting worse over a few months.

A deep jet-engine roar that is worst at high spin and has gradually worsened is most often worn drum bearings. A loose drum support or, less often, a belt/pulley fault can sound similar; roughness when turning and up-and-down play in the inner drum point strongly to the bearings/support. With the machine switched off and unplugged, empty it, open the door, turn the drum slowly by hand, then lift the inner drum from the top and check for a clunk or noticeable movement. If it is rough or has play, avoid high-speed spins and arrange an engineer assessment: bearing repairs usually require substantial dismantling.
Turned the drum by hand and it rumbles/grinds. Lifting the edge there's a noticeable clunky up and down play. Is it worth fixing on a 9 year old machine?

Possibly, but on a 9-year-old machine I would only repair it if the quote is reasonable and it is otherwise reliable. The grinding plus clunky vertical play makes worn drum bearings likely; a damaged drum support (spider) is the main alternative. Both are major strip-down repairs, and some machines have sealed tubs that make a bearing repair disproportionately expensive. Avoid high-speed spins meanwhile, as continued use can damage the drum, tub and seal further. Get a fixed diagnostic/repair quote, then compare it with a replacement; if the repair approaches roughly half the cost of a comparable new machine, replacement is usually the better value.
